text: Daya Ram Thapar (6 April 1894 – 15 December 1965) was an Indian Army medical officer and Director-General of the Indian Armed Forces Medical Services. Born into a prominent Punjabi family in Lahore, he received his early education there, including studies at Government College Lahore. He entered the University of Edinburgh in 1911 for medical studies, graduating with a Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery (M.B.Ch.B.) in 1916. He later obtained a diploma in tropical medicine and hygiene (DTM&H) from London and an M.D. from Edinburgh in 1930, with a thesis on ascariasis. While a student at Edinburgh, he organized the Scottish Wing of the Indian Volunteers' Ambulance Corps in 1914 following the outbreak of war, recruiting 120 Indian students to serve as dressers and interpreters. He was commissioned as a temporary lieutenant in the Indian Medical Service (IMS) on 25 March 1918, promoted to temporary captain on 25 March 1919, received a regular commission as a lieutenant on 14 March 1920, and was promoted to substantive captain on 25 March 1921. He was promoted to major on 25 September 1929, appointed staff captain (medical) on 1 July 1936, and promoted to lieutenant-colonel on 25 September 1937. On 14 October 1937, he was posted to Peshawar as second-in-command of a hospital and became the officiating Officer Commanding on 3 May 1938. He was posted to Rawalpindi on 15 June 1939 as Officer in Command of No. 1 Battalion Indian Hospital Corps. Assigned as Officer Commanding Indian Hospital Corps at Kirkee on 22 October 1942, he was promoted to acting colonel on 5 November 1942 and to temporary colonel on 5 May 1943 while serving as Commandant, Indian Army Medical Corps (IAMC) HQ at Pune. He was appointed a Companion of the Order of the Indian Empire (CIE) in the 1946 Birthday Honours and had previously received an Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE) in the 1942 New Year Honours. His final appointment prior to Indian independence was as deputy director of Medical Services, Medical Department. He was promoted to substantive colonel on 1 October 1946 (with seniority from 25 September 1940). Following Indian independence in 1947, he was promoted to major general on 3 September. On 1 January 1951, he was promoted to lieutenant general and appointed Director-General of the Armed Forces Medical Services, with an ex-officio appointment as a member of the Medical Council of India. He retired in 1954 and served as Colonel Commandant of the Army Medical Corps until April 1956. He died in New Delhi in December 1965. Thapar was the son of Dewan Bahadur Kunj Behari Thapar OBE; his younger brother was General Pran Nath Thapar, the future Chief of Staff of the Indian Army. He was the father of journalist Romesh Thapar and the noted author and historian Romila Thapar.
